1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-round-independence.sh: is an interview transcript asked in
     4	# prerequisite-ordered rounds?
     5	#
     6	# In `interview.pacing: rounds` every round of questions ends with one comment
     7	# block (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing):
     8	#
     9	#   <!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true}] -->
    10	#
    11	# This checker reads those blocks from a transcript (markdown or plain text,
    12	# one block per line) and fails when:
    13	#   * a `depends_on` names a question asked in the same round,
    14	#   * a `depends_on` names a question not asked in an earlier round,
    15	#   * a non-reasked id repeats, or a `reasked` id was never asked before,
    16	#   * round numbers do not increase, or a block is malformed,
    17	#   * the rounds average fewer than --min-average new questions (default 2).
    18	# `reasked` entries are skipped for id uniqueness and for the average. The
    19	# final round is exempt from the average when there are two or more rounds.
    20	#
    21	# Usage:
    22	#   tools/check-round-independence.sh <transcript> [--min-average N] [--json]
    23	#
    24	# Exit codes: 0 independent · 1 violation · 2 usage, unreadable file, or no
    25	#             round block in the transcript
    26	# =============================================================================
    27	set -euo pipefail
    28	export LC_ALL=C
    29	
    30	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    31	
    32	TRANSCRIPT=""
    33	MIN_AVG="2"
    34	JSON=0
    35	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    36	  case "$1" in
    37	    --min-average)
    38	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average needs a number" >&2; exit 2; }
    39	      MIN_AVG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    40	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    41	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    42	    --) shift; [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && { TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift; } ;;
    43	    -*) echo "check-round-independence.sh: unknown flag $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    44	    *)
    45	      [[ -z "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: one transcript only" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	      TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift ;;
    47	  esac
    48	done
    49	
    50	[[ -n "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: transcript path required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    51	[[ -f "$TRANSCRIPT" && -r "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: cannot read $TRANSCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }
    52	[[ "$MIN_AVG" =~ ^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average must be a non-negative number, got '$MIN_AVG'" >&2; exit 2; }
    53	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: jq is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	
    55	BLOCK_RE='<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*\[.*\][[:space:]]*-->'
    56	
    57	# One JSON object per block: {round, questions} or {round, malformed}. grep exits
    58	# 1 on no match, which is the "no block" case below, not an error.
    59	blocks="$(grep -oE "$BLOCK_RE" "$TRANSCRIPT" || true)"
    60	if [[ -z "$blocks" ]]; then
    61	  echo "check-round-independence.sh: no <!-- round: N; questions: [...] --> block in $TRANSCRIPT" >&2
    62	  exit 2
    63	fi
    64	
    65	rounds_json="[]"
    66	while IFS= read -r block; do
    67	  [[ -n "$block" ]] || continue
    68	  n="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+).*/\1/')"
    69	  [[ ${#n} -le 9 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: round number $n is too long" >&2; exit 1; }
    70	  n=$((10#$n))   # "02" is not valid JSON; the round number is decimal
    71	  arr="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*-->$//')"
    72	  if printf '%s' "$arr" | jq -e 'type == "array" and all(.[];
    73	        type == "object" and (.id | type == "string" and length > 0)
    74	        and (.depends_on | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string")))' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    75	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --argjson q "$arr" '{round: $r, questions: $q}')"
    76	  else
    77	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --arg raw "$arr" '{round: $r, malformed: $raw}')"
    78	  fi
    79	  rounds_json="$(jq -cn --argjson a "$rounds_json" --argjson e "$entry" '$a + [$e]')"
    80	done <<< "$blocks"
    81	
    82	report="$(jq -n --argjson rounds "$rounds_json" --argjson min "$MIN_AVG" '
    83	  reduce range(0; $rounds | length) as $i (
    84	    {asked: [], violations: [], per_round: [], prev: null};
    85	    $rounds[$i] as $r
    86	    | (if .prev != null and $r.round <= .prev
    87	         then .violations += ["round \($r.round) does not follow round \(.prev)"] else . end)
    88	    | .prev = $r.round
    89	    | if $r.malformed != null then
    90	        .violations += ["round \($r.round): malformed questions array (each entry needs a string id and a depends_on array of strings)"]
    91	        | .per_round += [{round: $r.round, new: 0, reasked: 0, ids: []}]
    92	      else
    93	        ($r.questions | map(.id)) as $here
    94	        | .asked as $before
    95	        | reduce $r.questions[] as $q (.;
    96	            ($q.reasked == true) as $re
    97	            | (if $re then
    98	                 (if ($before | index([$q.id])) == null
    99	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is marked reasked but was not asked in an earlier round"] else . end)
   100	               else
   101	                 (if (.asked | index([$q.id])) != null
   102	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is asked again without \"reasked\": true"] else . end)
   103	                 | .asked += [$q.id]
   104	               end)
   105	            | reduce $q.depends_on[] as $d (.;
   106	                if ($here | index([$d])) != null and $d != $q.id then
   107	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), asked in the same round"]
   108	                elif $d == $q.id then
   109	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on itself"]
   110	                elif ($before | index([$d])) == null then
   111	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), not asked in an earlier round"]
   112	                else . end))
   113	        | .per_round += [{
   114	            round: $r.round,
   115	            new: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked != true)) | length),
   116	            reasked: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked == true)) | length),
   117	            ids: $here }]
   118	      end)
   119	  | .counted = (if (.per_round | length) >= 2 then .per_round[0:-1] else .per_round end)
   120	  | .average = (if (.counted | length) == 0 then 0
   121	                else ((.counted | map(.new) | add) / (.counted | length)) end)
   122	  | (if .average < $min
   123	       then .violations += ["average \(.average * 100 | round / 100) new questions per round is below --min-average \($min)"] else . end)
   124	  | {
   125	      rounds: (.per_round | length),
   126	      questions: (.per_round | map(.new) | add),
   127	      reasked: (.per_round | map(.reasked) | add),
   128	      average: (.average * 100 | round / 100),
   129	      min_average: $min,
   130	      final_round_exempt: ((.per_round | length) >= 2),
   131	      per_round: .per_round,
   132	      violations: .violations,
   133	      verdict: (if (.violations | length) == 0 then "PASS" else "FAIL" end)
   134	    }')"
   135	
   136	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   137	  printf '%s\n' "$report"
   138	else
   139	  printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '
   140	    (.per_round[] | "round \(.round): \(.new) new question(s)\(if .reasked > 0 then ", \(.reasked) re-asked" else "" end) [\(.ids | join(" "))]"),
   141	    "rounds: \(.rounds); questions: \(.questions); average: \(.average) per round\(if .final_round_exempt then " (final round exempt)" else "" end); min-average: \(.min_average)",
   142	    (.violations[] | "VIOLATION: \(.)"),
   143	    .verdict'
   144	fi
   145	
   146	verdict="$(printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '.verdict')"
   147	[[ "$verdict" == "PASS" ]]

32:#   sha256_portable    Portable SHA-256 hashing (handles GNU sha256sum vs BSD shasum)
33-#
34-# Environment:
35-#   LOA_COMPAT_DEBUG=1   Enable debug output for platform detection
36-# =============================================================================
37-
38-# Prevent double-sourcing
39-if [[ "${_COMPAT_LIB_LOADED:-}" == "true" ]]; then
40-  return 0 2>/dev/null || exit 0
41-fi
42-_COMPAT_LIB_LOADED=true
43-
44-_COMPAT_LIB_VERSION="1.3.0"
--
93:# Empty string means neither is available — sha256_portable will fail loud at
94-# call time rather than at source time, so callers that don't need hashing can
95-# still source the library.
96-_COMPAT_SHA256_CMD=""
97-if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
98-  _COMPAT_SHA256_CMD="gnu"
99-elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
100-  _COMPAT_SHA256_CMD="bsd"
101-fi
102-
103-if [[ "${LOA_COMPAT_DEBUG:-}" == "1" ]]; then
104-  echo "[compat-lib] OS: $_COMPAT_OS" >&2
105-  echo "[compat-lib] sed: $_COMPAT_SED_STYLE" >&2
--
478:# sha256_portable - Portable SHA-256 hashing (sprint-bug-172 / bug-911)
479-# =============================================================================
480-#
481-# GNU coreutils ships `sha256sum`; macOS ships `shasum -a 256` (Perl-based
482-# from BSD's stock toolchain). Loa framework scripts that called raw
483-# sha256sum silently produced empty hashes on macOS, cascading into
484-# validation FAILs (e.g., butterfreezone-gen → butterfreezone-validate
485-# returning 10/12 instead of 12/12 provenance tagged).
486-#
487-# Argv shape matches sha256sum exactly: pass file paths positionally, or
488-# pipe content via stdin. Output format is byte-identical between GNU and
489-# BSD (`<hex-hash>  <filename-or-dash>` with two spaces), so downstream

+## Question Pacing
+
+One key, `interview.pacing`, sets the pacing for the discovery interview, `/architect` Phase 2, `/sprint-plan` Phase 2 and `/chart`. Those skills point here.
+
+| Pacing | Behavior |
+|---|---|
+| `sequential` | Ask ONE question per turn. Wait for response. Then ask the next. The supported opt-out from rounds. |
+| `batch` | Present 3-6 numbered questions. User responds to all at once. The `minimal` default. |
+| `rounds` | Ask the whole frontier per turn, as below. The `thorough` default. |
+
+### Rounds
+
+1. **Frontier.** The frontier is every open question whose prerequisites are settled. A question that depends on another question still open waits for a later round. There is no cap on round size.
+2. **Facts stay out.** A fact (what code, reality files or docs say) is looked up, never asked; only decisions enter a round (Backpressure Protocol, "Fact or decision").
+3. **Phase scope.** A round runs within the current discovery phase. A question that belongs to a later phase is parked for that phase. Phase gates are unchanged.
+4. **Format.** Number questions across the session (`Q1`, `Q2`, ...), so ids never restart. Each question has a short title line starting `❓ Q<n>:`, the question worded so that "yes" accepts the recommendation, and a `➡ Recommended:` line giving the answer and its reason, with a citation when there is one. Close the round with the answer prompt and the comment block.
+5. **Answers.** A bare "yes" accepts every recommendation in the round. A numbered answer (`2: no, keep it local`) overrides that question. If the operator answers some numbers and not others, restate the unanswered ones with their recommendations and ask for confirmation; they take the recommendation only after the operator confirms. A question still unconfirmed is re-asked in the next round.
+6. **Recompute.** Before the next round, recompute the frontier from the answers: settled questions leave, questions whose prerequisites just settled join. "wrap up" ends the phase.

+## Interview Modes
+
+The skill resolves `interview_mode` (`interview.mode`, overridden per skill by `interview.per_skill.<skill>`), `pacing` and the input styles in its Config Reading block. These tables say what each value does.
+
+### Mode Behavior Table
+
+| Mode | Questions/Phase | Default pacing | Phase Gates | Gap Skipping |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| `thorough` | 3-6 (scales down with context) | `rounds` | All ON | Always ask `min_confirm` |
+| `minimal` | 1-2 | `batch` | `before_generation` only | Skip covered phases |
+
+An explicit `interview.pacing` wins over the mode default, so a config that sets `sequential` keeps it.
+
+### Input Style Resolution
+
+| Interaction Type | `structured` | `plain` |
+|---|---|---|
+| Routing gates | AskUserQuestion with options | "Continue, go back, or skip ahead?" |
+| Discovery questions | AskUserQuestion with suggested answers | Markdown question, user responds freely |
+| Confirmations | AskUserQuestion (Yes/Correct/Adjust) | "Is this accurate? [yes/corrections]" |
+
+In `rounds` pacing, a round is one message even when `discovery_questions` is `structured`: present the numbered round as markdown and take the reply as text, because a round can hold more questions than one AskUserQuestion call allows.
+
+## Question Pacing
+
+One key, `interview.pacing`, sets the pacing for the discovery interview, `/architect` Phase 2, `/sprint-plan` Phase 2 and `/chart`. Those skills point here.
+
+| Pacing | Behavior |
+|---|---|
+| `sequential` | Ask ONE question per turn. Wait for response. Then ask the next. The supported opt-out from rounds. |
+| `batch` | Present 3-6 numbered questions. User responds to all at once. The `minimal` default. |
+| `rounds` | Ask the whole frontier per turn, as below. The `thorough` default. |
+
+### Rounds
+
+1. **Frontier.** The frontier is every open question whose prerequisites are settled. A question that depends on another question still open waits for a later round. There is no cap on round size.
+2. **Facts stay out.** A fact (what code, reality files or docs say) is looked up, never asked; only decisions enter a round (Backpressure Protocol, "Fact or decision").
+3. **Phase scope.** A round runs within the current discovery phase. A question that belongs to a later phase is parked for that phase. Phase gates are unchanged.
+4. **Format.** Number questions across the session (`Q1`, `Q2`, ...), so ids never restart. Each question has a short title line starting `❓ Q<n>:`, the question worded so that "yes" accepts the recommendation, and a `➡ Recommended:` line giving the answer and its reason, with a citation when there is one. Close the round with the answer prompt and the comment block.
+5. **Answers.** A bare "yes" accepts every recommendation in the round. A numbered answer (`2: no, keep it local`) overrides that question. If the operator answers some numbers and not others, restate the unanswered ones with their recommendations and ask for confirmation; they take the recommendation only after the operator confirms. A question still unconfirmed is re-asked in the next round.
+6. **Recompute.** Before the next round, recompute the frontier from the answers: settled questions leave, questions whose prerequisites just settled join. "wrap up" ends the phase.
+7. **Comment block.** End every round with one HTML comment holding a JSON array, one object per question: `{"id": "Q4", "depends_on": ["Q1"]}`. `depends_on` lists the earlier questions this one needed settled, `[]` when none. A re-asked question keeps its id and carries `"reasked": true`. The block is how `tools/check-round-independence.sh` checks that no question in a round depends on another question in the same round.
+
+```
+Round 2 (Functional Requirements)
+
+❓ Q4: Ledger location
+Should the decision ledger live at grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml, tracked?
+➡ Recommended: yes (the spec and two readers already point there; decision-lineage.md:23)
+
+❓ Q5: Unattended record
+Should unattended runs write a DEC row for every decision they take for you?
+➡ Recommended: yes (makes "which did a human decide?" answerable)
+
+❓ Q2: Default pacing (re-asked)
+Should rounds be the default pacing for thorough mode?
+➡ Recommended: yes (one turn per frontier instead of one per question)
+
+"yes" accepts all three; answer by number to override one.
+<!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q5","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true}] -->
+```
+
+The checker: `tools/check-round-independence.sh <transcript> [--min-average N] [--json]` exits 0 when every round is independent and the rounds average at least N questions (default 2; the final round is exempt when there are two or more rounds), 1 on a violation, 2 when the transcript has no round block.

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/check-round-independence.bats
+#
+# tools/check-round-independence.sh reads the `<!-- round: N; questions: [...] -->`
+# blocks that `interview.pacing: rounds` puts at the end of every round
+# (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing) and fails
+# when a question depends on another question of the same round, on one never
+# asked earlier, when ids repeat without "reasked", or when rounds average
+# fewer than --min-average new questions (final round exempt).
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-round-independence.sh"
+    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/rounds"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/transcript.md"
+}
+
+# Write a transcript whose rounds are the given JSON arrays, in order.
+transcript() {
+    local n=0 arr
+    : > "$T"
+    for arr in "$@"; do
+        n=$((n + 1))
+        printf 'Round %d\n\nquestions...\n<!-- round: %d; questions: %s -->\n\n' "$n" "$n" "$arr" >> "$T"
+    done
+}
+
+@test "RI-1 the independent fixture passes at the default minimum and reports per-round counts" {
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: 3 new question(s) [Q1 Q2 Q3]"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 3: 1 new question(s), 1 re-asked [Q6 Q7]"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"rounds: 4; questions: 8; average: 2.33 per round (final round exempt); min-average: 2"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"PASS"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-2 the fixture has at least three rounds and --json carries the report fields" {
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.rounds' <<< "$output")" -ge 3 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.verdict' <<< "$output")" = "PASS" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.min_average' <<< "$output")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.final_round_exempt' <<< "$output")" = "true" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.violations | length' <<< "$output")" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.per_round | length' <<< "$output")" -eq "$(jq -r '.rounds' <<< "$output")" ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-3 the negative fixture fails on its same-round dependency" {
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/same-round-dependency.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"VIOLATION: round 1: Q3 depends on Q2, asked in the same round"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"FAIL"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-4 a final one-question round does not lower the average" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q3","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q4","depends_on":["Q2"]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q5","depends_on":["Q3"]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.average' <<< "$output")" = "2" ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-5 a one-question round that is not the final round fails the default minimum" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q2","depends_on":["Q1"]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q3","depends_on":["Q2"]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"below --min-average 2"* ]]
+    run "$CHECK" "$T" --min-average 1
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-6 a single round is held to the minimum (no exemption with one round)" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.final_round_exempt' <<< "$output")" = "false" ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-7 reasked entries are ignored for uniqueness and the average" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q5","depends_on":["Q2"]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.questions' <<< "$output")" = "5" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.reasked' <<< "$output")" = "1" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.average' <<< "$output")" = "2" ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-8 a repeated id without reasked fails; reasked on a never-asked id fails" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'Q2 is asked again without "reasked": true'* ]]
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q9","depends_on":[],"reasked":true},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Q9 is marked reasked but was not asked in an earlier round"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-9 a dependency on an unknown or later question fails" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":["Q7"]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q7","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: Q1 depends on Q7, not asked in an earlier round"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-10 a self-dependency and a non-increasing round number fail" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Q1 depends on itself"* ]]
+    printf '%s\n' '<!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}] -->' \
+                  '<!-- round: 1; questions: [{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]}] -->' > "$T"
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 1 does not follow round 2"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-11 a malformed questions array is a violation, not a crash" {
+    printf '%s\n' '<!-- round: 1; questions: [{"id":"Q1"},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":"Q1"}] -->' \
+                  '<!-- round: 2; questions: [not json] -->' > "$T"
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: malformed questions array"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 2: malformed questions array"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-12 no round block exits 2; usage errors exit 2" {
+    printf 'an interview with no round blocks\n' > "$T"
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"no <!-- round: N; questions: [...] --> block"* ]]
+    run "$CHECK"
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    run "$CHECK" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/missing.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md" --min-average two
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md" --bogus
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-13 the REFERENCE.md worked example is itself a valid round" {
+    local ref="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md"
+    {
+        printf '%s\n' '<!-- round: 1; questions: [{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}] -->'
+        grep -E '^<!-- round: 2;' "$ref"
+    } > "$T"
+    [ "$(grep -c '^<!-- round: 2;' "$T")" -eq 1 ]
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/check-round-independence.bats
+#
+# tools/check-round-independence.sh reads the `<!-- round: N; questions: [...] -->`
+# blocks that `interview.pacing: rounds` puts at the end of every round
+# (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing) and fails
+# when a question depends on another question of the same round, on one never
+# asked earlier, when ids repeat without "reasked", or when rounds average
+# fewer than --min-average new questions (final round exempt).
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-round-independence.sh"
+    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/rounds"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/transcript.md"
+}
+
+# Write a transcript whose rounds are the given JSON arrays, in order.
+transcript() {
+    local n=0 arr
+    : > "$T"
+    for arr in "$@"; do
+        n=$((n + 1))
+        printf 'Round %d\n\nquestions...\n<!-- round: %d; questions: %s -->\n\n' "$n" "$n" "$arr" >> "$T"
+    done
+}
+
+@test "RI-1 the independent fixture passes at the default minimum and reports per-round counts" {
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: 3 new question(s) [Q1 Q2 Q3]"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 3: 1 new question(s), 1 re-asked [Q6 Q7]"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"rounds: 4; questions: 8; average: 2.33 per round (final round exempt); min-average: 2"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"PASS"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-2 the fixture has at least three rounds and --json carries the report fields" {
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.rounds' <<< "$output")" -ge 3 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.verdict' <<< "$output")" = "PASS" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.min_average' <<< "$output")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.final_round_exempt' <<< "$output")" = "true" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.violations | length' <<< "$output")" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.per_round | length' <<< "$output")" -eq "$(jq -r '.rounds' <<< "$output")" ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-3 the negative fixture fails on its same-round dependency" {
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/same-round-dependency.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"VIOLATION: round 1: Q3 depends on Q2, asked in the same round"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"FAIL"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-4 a final one-question round does not lower the average" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q3","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q4","depends_on":["Q2"]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q5","depends_on":["Q3"]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.average' <<< "$output")" = "2" ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-5 a one-question round that is not the final round fails the default minimum" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q2","depends_on":["Q1"]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q3","depends_on":["Q2"]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"below --min-average 2"* ]]
+    run "$CHECK" "$T" --min-average 1
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-6 a single round is held to the minimum (no exemption with one round)" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.final_round_exempt' <<< "$output")" = "false" ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-7 reasked entries are ignored for uniqueness and the average" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q5","depends_on":["Q2"]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.questions' <<< "$output")" = "5" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.reasked' <<< "$output")" = "1" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.average' <<< "$output")" = "2" ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-8 a repeated id without reasked fails; reasked on a never-asked id fails" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'Q2 is asked again without "reasked": true'* ]]
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q9","depends_on":[],"reasked":true},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Q9 is marked reasked but was not asked in an earlier round"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-9 a dependency on an unknown or later question fails" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":["Q7"]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
+               '[{"id":"Q7","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: Q1 depends on Q7, not asked in an earlier round"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-10 a self-dependency and a non-increasing round number fail" {
+    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]'
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Q1 depends on itself"* ]]
+    printf '%s\n' '<!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}] -->' \
+                  '<!-- round: 1; questions: [{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]}] -->' > "$T"
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 1 does not follow round 2"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-11 a malformed questions array is a violation, not a crash" {
+    printf '%s\n' '<!-- round: 1; questions: [{"id":"Q1"},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":"Q1"}] -->' \
+                  '<!-- round: 2; questions: [not json] -->' > "$T"
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: malformed questions array"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"round 2: malformed questions array"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RI-12 no round block exits 2; usage errors exit 2" {
+    printf 'an interview with no round blocks\n' > "$T"
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"no <!-- round: N; questions: [...] --> block"* ]]
+    run "$CHECK"
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    run "$CHECK" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/missing.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md" --min-average two
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md" --bogus
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+}
+
+@test "RI-13 the REFERENCE.md worked example is itself a valid round" {
+    local ref="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md"
+    {
+        printf '%s\n' '<!-- round: 1; questions: [{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}] -->'
+        grep -E '^<!-- round: 2;' "$ref"
+    } > "$T"
+    [ "$(grep -c '^<!-- round: 2;' "$T")" -eq 1 ]
+    run "$CHECK" "$T"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}

     3	# user-invoked-commands.bats: the operator-only command allowlist (FR-8, D-8.3)
     4	# =============================================================================
     5	# `.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt` lists commands carrying
     6	# `disable-model-invocation: true`. The harness refuses those to the Skill
     7	# tool (tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats), so no other command or skill
     8	# body may tell the model to run one as a step. Asserts:
     9	#   1. every listed command file exists and carries the flag
    10	#   2. no other body has an operative line for a listed name
    11	#   3. every command file carrying the flag is listed
    12	#   4. no SKILL.md allowed-tools grants dec-write-lib.sh confirm, supersede
    13	#      or context --clear (those are reachable only through /decisions)
    14	# Each check is a function over a root directory, proved against fixtures.
    15	
    16	setup() {
    17	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    18	    export LC_ALL=C
    19	}
    20	
    21	# list_names <root>: the allowlisted names, comments and blanks stripped
    22	list_names() {
    23	    sed -e 's/#.*$//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' \
    24	        "$1/.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt" | grep -v '^$' || true
    25	}
    26	
    27	# frontmatter <file>: the first YAML frontmatter block (empty when none)
    28	frontmatter() {
    29	    awk 'NR==1 && $0!="---"{exit} /^---[[:space:]]*$/{n++; if(n==2) exit; next} n==1{print}' "$1"
    30	}
    31	
    32	has_flag() {
    33	    frontmatter "$1" | grep -Eq '^disable-model-invocation:[[:space:]]*"?true"?[[:space:]]*$'
    34	}
    35	
    36	# check_listed_flagged <root>: prints each listed name whose file is missing or unflagged
    37	check_listed_flagged() {
    38	    local root="$1" name f
    39	    while IFS= read -r name; do
    40	        f="$root/.claude/commands/$name.md"
    41	        if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
    42	            echo "missing: $name"
    43	        elif ! has_flag "$f"; then
    44	            echo "unflagged: $name"
    45	        fi
    46	    done < <(list_names "$root")
    47	}
    48	
    49	# check_flagged_listed <root>: prints each flagged command file not in the list
    50	check_flagged_listed() {
    51	    local root="$1" f name names
    52	    names="$(list_names "$root")"
    53	    for f in "$root"/.claude/commands/*.md; do
    54	        [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    55	        has_flag "$f" || continue
    56	        name="$(basename "$f" .md)"
    57	        grep -qxF "$name" <<<"$names" || echo "unlisted: $name"
    58	    done
    59	}
    60	
    61	# check_operative <root>: prints file:line for each operative reference to a
    62	# listed name in a body other than that command's own file
    63	check_operative() {
    64	    local root="$1" name re exempt
    65	    exempt='(^|[^[:alpha:]])(user|operator|human|manually|suggest|recommend|tell|ask)'
    66	    while IFS= read -r name; do
    67	        # SDD D-8.3 pattern, widened: verbs match in any case and may take
    68	        # "the" ("execute /x", "Invoke the /x skill").
    69	        re="([Ee][Xx][Ee][Cc][Uu][Tt][Ee]|[Ii][Nn][Vv][Oo][Kk][Ee]|[Rr][Uu][Nn]|[Cc][Aa][Ll][Ll])[[:space:]]+(the[[:space:]]+)?\`?/${name}([^[:alnum:]_-]|\$)|Skill\\(.*${name}"
    70	        { find "$root/.claude/commands" -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null
    71	          find "$root/.claude/skills" -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null; } |
    72	        while IFS= read -r f; do
    73	            [[ "$f" == "$root/.claude/commands/$name.md" ]] && continue
    74	            grep -nE "$re" "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -viE "$exempt" |
    75	                sed "s|^|${f#"$root"/}:|" || true
    76	        done
    77	    done < <(list_names "$root")
    78	}
    79	
    80	# check_operator_ops <root>: prints SKILL.md files whose allowed-tools grant
    81	# an operator-only dec-write-lib.sh operation
    82	check_operator_ops() {
    83	    local root="$1" f
    84	    while IFS= read -r f; do
    85	        frontmatter "$f" | awk '/^allowed-tools:/{on=1; print; next} on && /^[[:space:]]+-|^[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]/{print; next} {on=0}' |
    86	            grep -Eq 'dec-write-lib\.sh[^,)]*(confirm|supersede|context[[:space:]]+--clear)' && echo "${f#"$root"/}"
    87	    done < <(find "$root/.claude/skills" -name SKILL.md -type f 2>/dev/null)
    88	    return 0
    89	}

    96	    printf -- '---\nname: beta\ndisable-model-invocation: true\n---\nRun `/alpha` from another command body.\n' > "$r/.claude/commands/beta.md"

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# dec-write-lib.bats: the decision-ledger writer (.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh).
     4	#
     5	# Hermetic: every test copies the writer, its validator and compat-lib into a fresh temp project
     6	# (its own git repo and .run), so the host's run state, the live ledger and the operator's session
     7	# never leak in. The live grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml of this repository is never written.
     8	# Seams: the CLI (subcommands, exit codes) and the ledger file after each operation.

    11	# An empty ledger carrying the tracked file's header only: fixtures never inherit live rows
    12	# (the live ledger is seeded in the main checkout).

    14	
    15	setup() {
    16	  BATS_TEST_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    17	  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    18	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
    19	  command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"

    22	        LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT LOA_DEC_NO_FLOCK LOA_DEC_LOCK_WAIT

    24	  mkdir -p "$T/.claude/scripts/lib" "$T/grimoires/loa"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# user-invoked-harness.bats: does `disable-model-invocation: true` hide a
     4	# command from the model's Skill tool? (FR-8, SDD D-8.4)
     5	# =============================================================================
     6	# One live `claude -p` run in a throwaway project holding two fixture commands:
     7	# `fixture-hidden` (flagged) and `fixture-visible` (control, unflagged). The
     8	# live run gets the Skill tool only, so it cannot read the fixture bodies or
     9	# run anything else, and it never sees a real Loa command.
    10	#
    11	# Outcomes of the live test:
    12	#   pass   the control ran (its marker reached the stream) and the hidden
    13	#          command did not (no Skill tool_use for it, or an error result,
    14	#          and its marker is absent everywhere)
    15	#   fail   the hidden marker reached the stream: the flag does not hide the
    16	#          command, so FR-8 is lint-only and G-7 partial
    17	#   skip   no `claude` on PATH; LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0; CLI error, timeout or
    18	#          unparsable output; or the control never ran (inconclusive)
    19	# Set LOA_HARNESS_OUT=<file> to keep the raw stream-json as evidence.
    20	# The classifier is also exercised offline against canned streams.
    21	
    22	HIDDEN_MARK="HIDDEN-RAN"
    23	VISIBLE_MARK="VISIBLE-RAN"
    24	
    25	# classify_stream <stream-json file>
    26	# Prints one of: verified | flag-does-not-hide | inconclusive-control | unparsable
    27	classify_stream() {
    28	    local stream="$1"
    29	    if ! jq -e -s 'length > 0' "$stream" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    30	        echo "unparsable"
    31	        return 0
    32	    fi
    33	    # Marker text anywhere in a tool result, an injected user message or the
    34	    # final result means that command's body was loaded into the session.
    35	    local hidden_seen visible_seen
    36	    hidden_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$HIDDEN_MARK" \
    37	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    38	    visible_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$VISIBLE_MARK" \
    39	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    40	    if [[ "$hidden_seen" == "true" ]]; then
    41	        echo "flag-does-not-hide"
    42	    elif [[ "$visible_seen" != "true" ]]; then
    43	        echo "inconclusive-control"
    44	    else
    45	        echo "verified"
    46	    fi
    47	}
    48	
    49	# skill_calls <stream-json file>: one line per Skill tool_use, "<name>\t<is_error>"
    50	skill_calls() {
    51	    jq -r -s '
    52	      ([.[] | select(.type == "user") | .message.content[]? | select(.type? == "tool_result")
    53	         | {key: .tool_use_id, value: ((.is_error // false) | tostring)}] | from_entries) as $res
    54	      | .[] | select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]?
    55	      | select(.type? == "tool_use" and .name == "Skill")
    56	      | "\(.input.skill // .input.command // .input.name // "?")\t\($res[.id] // "no-result")"' "$1"
    57	}
    58	
    59	write_fixture_project() {
    60	    local dir="$1"
    61	    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude/commands"
    62	    git -C "$dir" init -q
    63	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-hidden.md" <<'EOF'
    64	---
    65	name: fixture-hidden
    66	description: fixture
    67	disable-model-invocation: true
    68	---
    69	
    70	Reply with the single word HIDDEN-RAN
    71	EOF
    72	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-visible.md" <<'EOF'
    73	---
    74	name: fixture-visible
    75	description: fixture
    76	---
    77	
    78	Reply with the single word VISIBLE-RAN
    79	EOF
    80	}
    81	
    82	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    83	# Offline: the classifier over canned streams (always runs)
    84	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    85	
    86	@test "classifier: hidden refused, control ran -> verified" {
    87	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/ok.jsonl"
    88	    cat > "$s" <<'EOF'
    89	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t1","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"fixture-hidden"}}]}}
    90	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"t1","is_error":true,"content":"Unknown skill: fixture-hidden"}]}}
    91	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t2","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"fixture-visible"}}]}}
    92	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"t2","content":"Launching skill: fixture-visible"}]}}
    93	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reply with the single word VISIBLE-RAN"}]}}
    94	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","result":"VISIBLE-RAN"}
    95	EOF
    96	    run classify_stream "$s"
    97	    [ "$output" = "verified" ]
    98	    run skill_calls "$s"
    99	    [[ "$output" == *$'fixture-hidden\ttrue'* ]]
   100	    [[ "$output" == *$'fixture-visible\tfalse'* ]]
   101	}
   102	
   103	@test "classifier: hidden body reached the stream -> flag-does-not-hide" {
   104	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/leak.jsonl"
   105	    cat > "$s" <<'EOF'
   106	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t1","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"fixture-hidden"}}]}}
   107	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reply with the single word HIDDEN-RAN"}]}}
   108	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","result":"HIDDEN-RAN VISIBLE-RAN"}
   109	EOF
   110	    run classify_stream "$s"
   111	    [ "$output" = "flag-does-not-hide" ]
   112	}
   113	
   114	@test "classifier: control never ran -> inconclusive-control" {
   115	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/noctl.jsonl"
   116	    cat > "$s" <<'EOF'
   117	{"type":"result","subtype":"error_max_turns","result":""}
   118	EOF
   119	    run classify_stream "$s"
   120	    [ "$output" = "inconclusive-control" ]
   121	}
   122	
   123	@test "classifier: garbage output -> unparsable" {
   124	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/bad.jsonl"
   125	    printf 'not json at all\n' > "$s"
   126	    run classify_stream "$s"
   127	    [ "$output" = "unparsable" ]
   128	}
   129	
   130	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   131	# Live: one claude -p run against the fixture project
   132	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   133	
   134	@test "live harness: disable-model-invocation hides a command from the Skill tool" {
   135	    if [[ "${LOA_HARNESS_CHECK:-1}" == "0" ]]; then
   136	        skip "LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0"
   137	    fi
   138	    if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   139	        skip "claude CLI not on PATH"
   140	    fi
   141	    if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   142	        skip "jq or timeout missing"
   143	    fi
   144	
   145	    local proj="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
   146	    write_fixture_project "$proj"
   147	    local out="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stream.jsonl"
   148	    local prompt="Use the Skill tool to invoke the skill named fixture-hidden, then use the Skill tool to invoke the skill named fixture-visible. Follow whatever each skill tells you, and report each tool result verbatim."
   149	
   150	    local rc=0
   151	    ( cd "$proj" && env -u CLAUDECODE timeout 180 claude -p --max-turns 3 \
   152	        --tools Skill --output-format stream-json --verbose \
   153	        --no-session-persistence "$prompt" ) > "$out" 2>"$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stderr" || rc=$?
   154	    if [[ -n "${LOA_HARNESS_OUT:-}" ]]; then
   155	        cp "$out" "$LOA_HARNESS_OUT"
   156	    fi
   157	
   158	    local verdict
   159	    verdict="$(classify_stream "$out")"
   160	    echo "verdict=$verdict rc=$rc" >&3
   161	    skill_calls "$out" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/skill_call: /' >&3 || true
   162	
   163	    case "$verdict" in
   164	        unparsable)
   165	            skip "CLI error or unparsable output (rc=$rc): $(head -c 300 "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stderr")" ;;
   166	        inconclusive-control)
   167	            skip "inconclusive: control not invocable (rc=$rc)" ;;
   168	        flag-does-not-hide)
   169	            echo "flag does not hide the command: FR-8 is lint-only, G-7 partial" >&2
   170	            return 1 ;;
   171	        verified)
   172	            return 0 ;;
   173	    esac
   174	    echo "unknown verdict: $verdict" >&2
   175	    return 1
   176	}
======

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# user-invoked-harness.bats: does `disable-model-invocation: true` hide a
     4	# command from the model's Skill tool? (FR-8, SDD D-8.4)
     5	# =============================================================================
     6	# One live `claude -p` run in a throwaway project holding two fixture commands:
     7	# `fixture-hidden` (flagged) and `fixture-visible` (control, unflagged). The
     8	# live run gets the Skill tool only, so it cannot read the fixture bodies or
     9	# run anything else, and it never sees a real Loa command.
    10	#
    11	# Outcomes of the live test:
    12	#   pass   the control ran (its marker reached the stream) and the hidden
    13	#          command did not (no Skill tool_use for it, or an error result,
    14	#          and its marker is absent everywhere)
    15	#   fail   the hidden marker reached the stream: the flag does not hide the
    16	#          command, so FR-8 is lint-only and G-7 partial
    17	#   skip   no `claude` on PATH; LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0; CLI error, timeout or
    18	#          unparsable output; or the control never ran (inconclusive)
    19	# Set LOA_HARNESS_OUT=<file> to keep the raw stream-json as evidence.
    20	# The classifier is also exercised offline against canned streams.
    21	
    22	HIDDEN_MARK="HIDDEN-RAN"
    23	VISIBLE_MARK="VISIBLE-RAN"
    24	
    25	# classify_stream <stream-json file>
    26	# Prints one of: verified | flag-does-not-hide | inconclusive-control | unparsable
    27	classify_stream() {
    28	    local stream="$1"
    29	    if ! jq -e -s 'length > 0' "$stream" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    30	        echo "unparsable"
    31	        return 0
    32	    fi
    33	    # Marker text anywhere in a tool result, an injected user message or the
    34	    # final result means that command's body was loaded into the session.
    35	    local hidden_seen visible_seen
    36	    hidden_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$HIDDEN_MARK" \
    37	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    38	    visible_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$VISIBLE_MARK" \
    39	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    40	    if [[ "$hidden_seen" == "true" ]]; then
    41	        echo "flag-does-not-hide"
    42	    elif [[ "$visible_seen" != "true" ]]; then
    43	        echo "inconclusive-control"
    44	    else
    45	        echo "verified"
    46	    fi
    47	}
    48	
    49	# skill_calls <stream-json file>: one line per Skill tool_use, "<name>\t<is_error>"
    50	skill_calls() {
    51	    jq -r -s '
    52	      ([.[] | select(.type == "user") | .message.content[]? | select(.type? == "tool_result")
    53	         | {key: .tool_use_id, value: ((.is_error // false) | tostring)}] | from_entries) as $res
    54	      | .[] | select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]?
    55	      | select(.type? == "tool_use" and .name == "Skill")
    56	      | "\(.input.skill // .input.command // .input.name // "?")\t\($res[.id] // "no-result")"' "$1"
    57	}
    58	
    59	write_fixture_project() {
    60	    local dir="$1"
    61	    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude/commands"
    62	    git -C "$dir" init -q
    63	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-hidden.md" <<'EOF'
    64	---
    65	name: fixture-hidden
    66	description: fixture
    67	disable-model-invocation: true
    68	---
    69	
    70	Reply with the single word HIDDEN-RAN
    71	EOF
    72	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-visible.md" <<'EOF'
    73	---
    74	name: fixture-visible
    75	description: fixture
    76	---
    77	
    78	Reply with the single word VISIBLE-RAN
    79	EOF
    80	}
    81	
    82	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    83	# Offline: the classifier over canned streams (always runs)
    84	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    85	
    86	@test "classifier: hidden refused, control ran -> verified" {
    87	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/ok.jsonl"
    88	    cat > "$s" <<'EOF'
    89	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t1","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"fixture-hidden"}}]}}
    90	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"t1","is_error":true,"content":"Unknown skill: fixture-hidden"}]}}
    91	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t2","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"fixture-visible"}}]}}
    92	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"t2","content":"Launching skill: fixture-visible"}]}}
    93	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reply with the single word VISIBLE-RAN"}]}}
    94	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","result":"VISIBLE-RAN"}
    95	EOF
    96	    run classify_stream "$s"
    97	    [ "$output" = "verified" ]
    98	    run skill_calls "$s"
    99	    [[ "$output" == *$'fixture-hidden\ttrue'* ]]
   100	    [[ "$output" == *$'fixture-visible\tfalse'* ]]
   101	}
   102	
   103	@test "classifier: hidden body reached the stream -> flag-does-not-hide" {
   104	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/leak.jsonl"
   105	    cat > "$s" <<'EOF'
   106	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t1","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"fixture-hidden"}}]}}
   107	{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reply with the single word HIDDEN-RAN"}]}}
   108	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","result":"HIDDEN-RAN VISIBLE-RAN"}
   109	EOF
   110	    run classify_stream "$s"
   111	    [ "$output" = "flag-does-not-hide" ]
   112	}
   113	
   114	@test "classifier: control never ran -> inconclusive-control" {
   115	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/noctl.jsonl"
   116	    cat > "$s" <<'EOF'
   117	{"type":"result","subtype":"error_max_turns","result":""}
   118	EOF
   119	    run classify_stream "$s"
   120	    [ "$output" = "inconclusive-control" ]
   121	}
   122	
   123	@test "classifier: garbage output -> unparsable" {
   124	    local s="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/bad.jsonl"
   125	    printf 'not json at all\n' > "$s"
   126	    run classify_stream "$s"
   127	    [ "$output" = "unparsable" ]
   128	}
   129	
   130	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   131	# Live: one claude -p run against the fixture project
   132	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   133	
   134	@test "live harness: disable-model-invocation hides a command from the Skill tool" {
   135	    if [[ "${LOA_HARNESS_CHECK:-1}" == "0" ]]; then
   136	        skip "LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0"
   137	    fi
   138	    if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   139	        skip "claude CLI not on PATH"
   140	    fi
   141	    if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   142	        skip "jq or timeout missing"
   143	    fi
   144	
   145	    local proj="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
   146	    write_fixture_project "$proj"
   147	    local out="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stream.jsonl"
   148	    local prompt="Use the Skill tool to invoke the skill named fixture-hidden, then use the Skill tool to invoke the skill named fixture-visible. Follow whatever each skill tells you, and report each tool result verbatim."
   149	
   150	    local rc=0
   151	    ( cd "$proj" && env -u CLAUDECODE timeout 180 claude -p --max-turns 3 \
   152	        --tools Skill --output-format stream-json --verbose \
   153	        --no-session-persistence "$prompt" ) > "$out" 2>"$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stderr" || rc=$?
   154	    if [[ -n "${LOA_HARNESS_OUT:-}" ]]; then
   155	        cp "$out" "$LOA_HARNESS_OUT"
   156	    fi
   157	
   158	    local verdict
   159	    verdict="$(classify_stream "$out")"
   160	    echo "verdict=$verdict rc=$rc" >&3
   161	    skill_calls "$out" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/skill_call: /' >&3 || true
   162	
   163	    case "$verdict" in
   164	        unparsable)
   165	            skip "CLI error or unparsable output (rc=$rc): $(head -c 300 "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stderr")" ;;
   166	        inconclusive-control)
   167	            skip "inconclusive: control not invocable (rc=$rc)" ;;
   168	        flag-does-not-hide)
   169	            echo "flag does not hide the command: FR-8 is lint-only, G-7 partial" >&2
   170	            return 1 ;;
   171	        verified)
   172	            return 0 ;;
   173	    esac
   174	    echo "unknown verdict: $verdict" >&2
   175	    return 1
   176	}

--- a/tests/unit/validate-artifact.bats

+
+# =============================================================================
+# decisions (the decision ledger) + the prd tag-to-row rule + the sdd DEC column
+# =============================================================================
+# Hermetic: a temp project under BATS_TEST_TMPDIR holds a copy of the validator, the ledger writer
+# and compat-lib, so the host's run state (a RUNNING run makes the context unattended) never leaks
+# in. Fixtures are written by the writer, then mutated by yq as a hand edit would be.
+
+_dec_skip_unless_tools() {
+    skip_if_no_jq
+    [[ "$(yq --version 2>&1)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]] || skip "Mike Farah yq v4 not installed"
+}
+
+_dec_project() {
+    unset LOA_UNATTENDED LOA_FLATLINE_MODE CI GITHUB_ACTIONS LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT CLAUDE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID
+    DP="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/dproj"

+    git -C "$DP" init -q
+    DV="$DP/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
+    DW="$DP/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh"
+    DL="$DP/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
+    DALT='{"option":"keep sequential","rejected_because":"slow"}'
+}
+# _dec_rows N: N proposed rows in the fixture ledger; DEC-0001 confirmed by the operator when $1 == confirm
+_dec_new_prop() { bash "$DW" new --file "$DL" --summary "${1:-rounds is the default}" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by t \
+    --source "${2:-prd.md#e (D1)}" --status proposed --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$DALT" --cycle cycle-128 --quiet; }
+_dec_confirm() { bash "$DW" confirm --file "$DL" --id "$1" --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence "cli:2026-10-13T12:00:00Z" --answer-ref "cli:2026-10-13T12:00:00Z" --quiet; }
+
+@test "validate-artifact decisions: the live ledger passes" {

+    run "$SCRIPT" --type decisions --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+

+    _dec_skip_unless_tools; _dec_project
+    _dec_new_prop >/dev/null; _dec_new_prop >/dev/null; _dec_new_prop >/dev/null
+    _dec_confirm DEC-0001
+    bash "$DW" reject --file "$DL" --id DEC-0002 --rationale no --follow-up bd-x --recorded-by t --quiet
+    bash "$DW" supersede --file "$DL" --id DEC-0001 --summary s2 --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by decisions-command --source s --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$DALT" --quiet >/dev/null

+_dec_bad() {
+    local expr="$1" want="$2" base="${3:-}"
+    cp "$DL" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/base.yaml"

+    [[ "$output" == *"$want"* ]] || { echo "missing [$want] in: $output"; return 1; }

+}

content.content:
### DISS-001 [BLOCKING] voice=gpt-5.5-pro anchor=.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:op_supersede
TITLE: 
DESC: Rejecting a proposed replacement leaves the original decision's supersede_proposed_by pointing to that rejected row. This guard then refuses every subsequent agent replacement proposal.
FAIL: After an agent proposes B to supersede decided row A and the operator rejects B, A remains decided but cannot receive another agent replacement proposal without manual repair or an operator override.
FIX: When rejecting a replacement, clear the original row's matching supersede_proposed_by atomically, or make this guard block only replacements that remain proposed.

### DISS-002 [BLOCKING] voice=gpt-5.5-pro anchor=.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:op_import
TITLE: 
DESC: Import locks only the destination ledger, snapshots the pending file, and later deletes that source without coordinating with its writers.
FAIL: A worktree writer can successfully append a pending row after import reads the source but before this deletion. Import commits only its earlier snapshot, then deletes the newly appended row without importing it.
FIX: Coordinate import and pending writes through a shared source lock held through source removal. Ensure the lock identity is shared across the main checkout and linked worktrees.

### DISS-C-001 [BLOCKING] voice=claude-headless anchor=.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:op_confirm
TITLE: 
DESC: `ctx_signals` emits a non-live `prd prd-status:` signal whenever grimoires/loa/prd.md has a `**Status**` line containing 'autonomous' or 'unattended'. `is_unattended` treats that signal exactly like a live run signal. `op_confirm` deliberately only refuses on `live_run_signal`, so it proceeds under a PRD signal, but it then calls `derive_attribution 0`, whose first branch (`if is_unattended`) discards `--answer-ref` with a WARN and leaves REF empty. The confirm jq then sets `.decided_by = (if decided_by_ref tests OPREF then "operator" else .proposed_by end)`, which resolves to the agent voice. The same `is_unattended` check also makes `op_reject` die on a decided row ('context is unattended') and makes `op_supersede` by the operator fall into the agent path (sets `supersede_proposed_by` instead of superseding). The /decisions command doc states the cli ref 'is what records decided_by: operator', so this is a spec violation that persists for the whole project lifetime once the PRD status mentions autonomy.
FAIL: An operator typing `/decisions confirm --id DEC-0007` in an interactive session with a PRD marked autonomous gets a ledger row with `status: decided`, `decided_by: agent`, no operator ref, and `transitions[].by: operator:decisions-command`. The `list --not-decided-by operator` SDD appendix then keeps reporting the row as an agent decision after the operator approved it, and `reject` on decided rows is permanently refused.
FIX: Split the signal kinds: in `derive_attribution`, only drop `--answer-ref`/`--as` when `live_run_signal` is true (or when the caller is not `is_operator_call`), and use `live_run_signal` instead of `is_unattended` in the operator branches of `op_reject` and `op_supersede`. Keep `is_unattended` (live + prd) only for deciding the landing status in `op_new`. Add a bats case: PRD with `**Status:** Autonomous`, interactive env, confirm with a cli ref, assert `decided_by == operator`.

### DISS-C-002 [ADVISORY] voice=claude-headless anchor=.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:resolve_target
TITLE:

head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:313 — derive_attribution drops the operator's --answer-ref whenever is_unattended is true, and is_unattended includes the non-live PRD `**Status:** ... autonomous|unattended` signal (lines 177-180). op_confirm (line 509) deliberately lets that signal through, so an interactive `/decisions confirm --answer-ref cli:...` on a project whose PRD mentions an autonomous run lands `status: decided, decided_by: agent, decided_by_ref: null` (jq at lines 536-538); the operator's approval is recorded as the agent deciding, and validate-artifact.sh accepts it because transitions[].by is hard-coded operator:decisions-command (line 536). Reproduced. The same branch makes op_reject write `by: agent:decisions-command` for an operator rejection (line 572), refuses the operator rejecting a decided row (line 575) and sends an operator supersede down the agent path (lines 600-611). tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:354-366 exercises this scenario but asserts only `status`.
head/tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:28 — every ledger suite seeds its fixture from the repository's grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml (also validate-artifact.bats:630 and :644, grimoire-index.bats:80), .gitignore:150 re-includes it and validate-gitignore-state.sh:58 declares it tracked, but the change never adds that file. On a checkout without it, setup fails for 44/44 dec-write-lib tests (`sed: can't read .../decisions.yaml`, verified), the grimoire-index decisions tests and "the live ledger passes" fail, and the writer's live path dies at dec-write-lib.sh:271. The base .gitignore ignored the path, so a seeded, tracked ledger must land with this change.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:655 — op_import reads the pending file (line 629), appends its snapshot to the live ledger, then `rm -f`s the pending file without ever locking it; locks are keyed under each checkout's own .run (line 207), so a linked-worktree writer appending a PEND row between the read and the delete loses that row silently. Re-read the file before deleting and refuse when ids differ, or lock the pending file by a path both checkouts share.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:601 — after the operator rejects a proposed replacement, the superseded-candidate row keeps supersede_proposed_by pointing at the rejected row, so every later agent `supersede` of that decision is refused with "a replacement is already proposed" (reproduced); only an operator supersede can move it, and the append-only rules forbid clearing the field. Guard only on a replacement that is still proposed, or clear the pointer in op_reject.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:359 — is_operator_call is a string compare on --recorded-by; any Bash-capable agent can pass `--recorded-by decisions-command` and self-confirm rows as the operator. decisions.md:26 states the model "cannot invoke it", which overstates the boundary (the flag only hides the slash command from the Skill tool; the bats greps catch committed text, not ad-hoc tool calls). Document the real boundary or add a check an agent cannot forge from Bash (e.g. `[[ -t 0 ]]`).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:509 — a fresh unattended marker written by `context --set-unattended` in the same session stays `fresh` for unattended_marker_ttl_hours (24 h), so `/decisions confirm` is refused for the rest of the day after the run finishes; the refusal text does not mention `clear-unattended`, and decisions.md:109 documents that action only for stale markers.
head/tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats:151 — a unit-test suite runs a live, billable `claude -p` call (up to 180 s) by default whenever `claude` is on PATH; the opt-out is LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0. Make the live run opt-in.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:527 — validate_decisions is ~200 lines around a single ~120-line jq program (lines 568-689) and op_confirm (dec-write-lib.sh:506-558) is 53 lines; both exceed the 50-line function guideline without a justification comment.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:262 — the pending-file skeleton is written with `cat >` before acquire_lock (line 468); two worktree writers racing on a new pending file can have the slower skeleton truncate the faster writer's appended row.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:694 — `list --format md` prints "_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._" for every empty result, including `--id` of an unknown row or `--status decided --voice agent` (reproduced); the sentence is only true for the PR-body query.
head/.claude/scripts/grimoire-index.sh:217 — the INDEX.md intro still enumerates "(KF · vision · lore · handoff · observation)": the decisions family added here is missing and the observation family was removed in cycle-121.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:734 — BARE_ASSUMPTION_FAILS_FROM="2026-11-13" is a hard-coded date switch: bare [ASSUMPTION] tags turn from WARN to FAIL for PRDs dated on or after it with no config knob and no mention in .loa.config.yaml.example.
head/README.md:125 — the command total is bumped to 50 and points to PROCESS.md "for all commands", but PROCESS.md is not in the change; the new /decisions command is likely missing from that list.
head/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md:1 — the implementation report (PR.md) is two lines with no AC Verification walkthrough, no stated assumptions and no record of which test suites were run.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)
**Change under review:** `pr/head.diff` (39 files; sprint-252 decision surfaces, part 1). Citations are `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers from `pr/head/`.

---

## Overall Assessment

The change is substantial and mostly careful: the ledger writer (`dec-write-lib.sh`) keeps values out of yq expressions via `env()`, copies-verifies-renames every write, derives attribution instead of accepting it, and the session-start surface sanitises agent-authored rows inside the L6 fence. The 44-test writer suite, the validator suite and the round-independence checker are hermetic and pass when run against the PR head on a scratch repository that carries a seeded ledger.

Three defects block merge. First, the writer's attribution path treats the static PRD `**Status:**` signal like a live unattended run, so an interactive operator confirm on any project whose PRD mentions an autonomous run is recorded as `decided_by: agent` (reproduced; the validator accepts the result). Second, the change declares `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` tracked, re-includes it in `.gitignore`, and seeds every ledger test from the repository copy, but never adds that file; on a checkout without it the whole writer suite fails at setup and the live writer dies. Third, `import` deletes a linked worktree's pending file without locking it, so a row appended during the import is lost silently.

The cross-model dissent ran with two voices (gpt-5.5-pro primary, claude-headless companion) and independently raised the attribution defect, the import race and the stuck-supersede state; its findings are folded in below with their `DISS-` ids.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Attribution: operator confirm recorded as an agent decision under a PRD "autonomous" Status line

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:313` — `derive_attribution` discards the operator's `--answer-ref` whenever `is_unattended` is true, and `is_unattended` includes the non-live `prd prd-status:` signal (lines 177-180). `op_confirm` deliberately gates only on `live_run_signal` (line 509), so the confirm proceeds and the jq at lines 536-538 sets `decided_by = .proposed_by`.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:313` (also `:177-180`, `:509`, `:536-538`, `:572`, `:575`, `:600-611`)
**Issue:** Reproduced against the PR writer with a one-row ledger and a PRD containing `**Status:** Draft, autonomous run`, confirming exactly as `decisions.md` rule 3 instructs (`--evidence cli:<now> --answer-ref cli:<now>`):

```
dec-write: WARN: unattended context: --answer-ref ignored (the row stays proposed with proposed_by agent until /decisions confirm)
confirming DEC-0001: row1
dec-write: confirmed DEC-0001
exit=0
{"status":"decided","decided_by":"agent","decided_by_ref":null,"by":"operator:decisions-command"}
validator exit=0
```

The WARN text is also wrong for this path (the row does not stay proposed; it is confirmed). The same `is_unattended` branch makes `op_reject` record `by: agent:decisions-command` for an operator rejection (line 572, reproduced), refuses the operator rejecting a decided row at all (line 575), and sends an operator `supersede` down the agent path (lines 600-611: sets `supersede_proposed_by` instead of superseding). `validate-artifact.sh` cannot catch any of this because the writer hard-codes `transitions[].by = operator:decisions-command` (line 536), which is all the validator's `-> decided` rule checks (`head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:632`). The existing test `head/tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:354-366` exercises precisely this scenario but asserts only `status`, not `decided_by`.
**Why This Matters:** `decisions.md:55` promises "That operator-kind reference is what records `decided_by: operator`". The PRD signal is a static property of the project, so once a PRD mentions autonomy every operator confirmation for the rest of the cycle is misattributed, and `list --not-decided-by operator` (the PRD/SDD appendix and the PR body section) keeps reporting operator-approved rows as agent decisions. This is the one property the ledger exists to make answerable. Matches dissent DISS-C-001 (BLOCKING).
**Required Fix:** In `derive_attribution`, drop `--answer-ref`/`--as` only under `live_run_signal` (or only when the caller is not `is_operator_call`); use `live_run_signal` rather than `is_unattended` in the operator branches of `op_reject` (lines 572, 575) and `op_supersede` (lines 600, 606). Keep `is_unattended` (live + PRD) solely for choosing the landing status in `op_new` (line 467). Extend the bats case at `:354-366` to assert `decided_by == operator` and `decided_by_ref == cli:...` after the PRD-signal confirm, and add the reject/supersede counterparts.

### 2. The tracked ledger the change depends on is not in the change

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:28` — every ledger suite seeds its fixture from `$REPO/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`, `.gitignore` re-includes that path, `validate-gitignore-state.sh` declares it tracked, and the writer tells users to "restore the tracked" copy, yet the 39-file diff never adds the file.
**File:** `head/tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:28` (also `head/tests/unit/validate-artifact.bats:630`, `:644`; `head/tests/unit/grimoire-index.bats:80`; `head/.gitignore:150`; `head/.claude/scripts/validate-gitignore-state.sh:58`; `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:271`)
**Issue:** The base `.gitignore` ignored `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` (`pr/base/.gitignore:149`), so unless the base tree already carries a force-added copy, a fresh clone has no ledger. I ran the suites on the PR head without the file: `dec-write-lib.bats` fails 44/44 in `setup` (`sed: can't read .../grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`), the four `grimoire-index decisions:` tests and `validate-artifact decisions: the live ledger passes` fail, and `dec-write-lib.sh new` on the live path dies with "ledger not found ... (restore the tracked grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml)". With a seeded header-only ledger everything passes (44/44, 51/51, 13/13, 8/8, 12/12). The test at `dec-write-lib.bats:109-113` additionally requires the seeded file's first line to be the comment `# grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml: the decision ledger ...`, which nothing in the change provides.
**Why This Matters:** The feature is unusable on a fresh checkout and the suite that proves it is red in CI; the `.gitignore` negation (`head/.gitignore:150`) is a no-op without the file it re-includes.
**Required Fix:** Add the seeded `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` (header comment, `schema_version: 1`, `decisions: []`) to the change and confirm it is tracked (`git ls-files grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`). If the base tree already tracks it, say so in the report and drop the "restore" guidance; the confidence on this finding is medium only because the base tree outside the touched files is not visible here.

### 3. `import` deletes an unlocked pending file: rows appended during the import are lost

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:655` — `op_import` snapshots the pending file (`read_ledger "$from"`, line 629), appends that snapshot to the live ledger, then runs `rm -f -- "$from"` without ever holding a lock on the pending file.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:655` (also `:629`, `:207`)
**Issue:** The only lock taken is on the live ledger (line 628). Locks are keyed under *this checkout's* `.run` (`lock_path`, line 207), so even the worktree writer's own lock on the pending file lives in a different directory and is never contended by the importing main checkout. A linked-worktree agent that appends a PEND row between line 629 and line 655 (the design explicitly supports parallel sprint tasks in worktrees) has that row deleted with the file; the import output lists only the rows read earlier and nothing reports the loss.
**Why This Matters:** Silent loss of a decision row defeats the append-only guarantee the rest of the writer enforces so carefully. Matches dissent DISS-002 (BLOCKING) and DISS-C-003.
**Required Fix:** After `verify_and_swap`, re-read `$from` and refuse to delete it when its ids differ from the imported set (print the leftover ids and leave the file), or lock the pending file under a lock path derived from the pending file's own directory so both checkouts contend on the same lock. Add a bats case that appends to the pending file between read and delete (e.g. via a `yq -i` hook or a second writer) and asserts the row survives.

---

## Observations

### 1. Ledger state machine

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:601` — after the operator rejects a proposed replacement, the superseded-candidate row keeps `supersede_proposed_by` pointing at the rejected row, so every later agent `supersede` of that decision dies with "a replacement is already proposed" (reproduced: `supersede` -> `reject` -> second `supersede` exits 1). The append-only rules forbid clearing the pointer, so only an operator `supersede` can move the row. Dissent DISS-001 rated this BLOCKING; I rate it medium because the operator path still works, but the guard should consider only replacements that are still `proposed`, or `op_reject` should clear the pointer on the superseded-candidate row in the same write.
**Suggestion:** Guard on `$byid[.supersede_proposed_by].status == "proposed"` (and relax the validator's content-edit rule at `validate-artifact.sh:681` accordingly if the pointer is cleared).
**Benefit:** Agents can re-propose after an operator rejection without manual intervention.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:509` — a marker written by `context --set-unattended` in the current session stays `fresh` for `unattended_marker_ttl_hours` (24 h) as long as the session id matches, so after an autonomous run finishes the operator in the same session is refused `confirm` for the rest of the day. The refusal text ("confirm after the run, interactively") gives no repair step, and `decisions.md:109` documents `clear-unattended` only for markers the surface reports stale. Dissent DISS-C-005.
**Suggestion:** Have the run-mode completion/halt path clear or expire the marker, and name `/decisions clear-unattended` in the refusal message.
**Benefit:** The operator is never locked out of the confirm path by a finished run.

### 2. Trust boundary

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:359` — `is_operator_call` is a string compare on `--recorded-by`. Any Bash-capable agent can run `dec-write-lib.sh confirm ... --recorded-by decisions-command --answer-ref cli:...` and self-confirm its rows as the operator. `head/.claude/commands/decisions.md:26` says `disable-model-invocation: true` "keeps the model from starting it" and the description says "the model cannot invoke it", which overstates the boundary: the flag hides the slash command from the Skill tool, and the bats greps in `user-invoked-commands.bats` catch committed text, not ad-hoc tool calls. Dissent DISS-C-004. CWE-284 (improper access control), accepted-design territory but the doc should state the real boundary.
**Suggestion:** Either document that the operator-only property is enforced by convention plus static lint, or add a check an agent cannot forge from Bash (e.g. `[[ -t 0 ]]` for `confirm`, `reject`/`supersede` on a decided row and `context --clear`).
**Benefit:** Readers of `decisions.md` and the ledger know what `decided_by: operator` actually proves.

### 3. Tests

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats:151` — a unit-test suite runs a live, billable `claude -p` call (up to 180 s, `--max-turns 3`) by default whenever `claude` is on PATH; the opt-out is `LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0` (line 135). A non-hermetic network call in `tests/unit/` will surprise contributors and CI runners that have the CLI installed.
**Suggestion:** Make the live run opt-in (`LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=1`) or move it under an `integration`/`live` tag; keep the offline classifier tests where they are.
**Benefit:** `bats tests/unit` stays fast, deterministic and free.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md:1` — the implementation report is the two-line PR description: no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, no stated assumptions, no record of which suites were run or of the seeded-ledger prerequisite (Think Before Coding). Under the skill's rules a missing AC Verification section is itself an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED; it is recorded here as an observation because the verdict is already determined by the findings above.
**Suggestion:** Add an AC Verification section with `file:line` evidence per acceptance criterion and the exact test commands run.
